newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Duiker halts some operations after killing.
newsitem.headline: Duiker halts some operations after killing.

text.p: South Africa's Duiker Mining said on Thursday it had suspended operations at the Waterpan and Boschmans sections of its Tweefontein Collieries following the mob-killing of a mine manager on Wednesday.

On Wednesday Waterpan's mine manager Fanie Venter was set upon by several hundred people -- believed to be Tweefontein employees -- who torched his car and office before assaulting him and pushing him into his blazing vehicle.
He later died from the burns and injuries inflicted in the attack.

"We have suspended operations indefinitely at the Waterpan and neighbouring Boschmans collieries and there will be no return to work until the situation at the mine is back to normal and there is no longer a threat of any further violence," Hugh Stoyell, the group's managing director said.
He said management would meet with union and association representatives on Thursday morning to discuss the incident and attempt to establish the underlying reasons behind the attack.
Tweefontein Collieries is a division of Duiker Mining, which is a member of the Lonrho plc group of companies.
Its three operating sections -- Waterpan, Boschmans and WitCons -- mined over 7-million tons last year, from which 5.5 million tons of bituminous coal were produced.
